questions.title: Losartan's advantage over enalapril: less angioedema
questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of losartan over enalapril?

options.A: Better efficacy in lower blood pressure
options.B: Better prevention of secondary myocardial events

explanations.A: Incorrect. Losartan (an ARB) and enalapril (an ACE inhibitor) are comparably effective at lowering blood pressure; superior antihypertensive efficacy is not losartan's distinguishing advantage.
explanations.B: Incorrect. ACE inhibitors such as enalapril have well-established evidence for preventing secondary myocardial events; this is not an advantage that favours losartan over enalapril.
explanations.C: Correct. Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) such as losartan do not affect bradykinin metabolism, since they act downstream at the angiotensin II receptor rather than inhibiting the ACE enzyme that also degrades bradykinin. This gives losartan a lower incidence of angioedema than an ACE inhibitor such as enalapril, even though the two classes are otherwise comparable in efficacy for lowering blood pressure. Losartan has not been shown to be superior at preventing secondary myocardial events or to cost less.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Losartan is not generally the lower-cost option compared with enalapril; cost is not the basis of its advantage.

questions.learning_objective: State that losartan's chief advantage over enalapril is a lower incidence of angioedema, because ARBs do not inhibit bradykinin degradation the way ACE inhibitors do.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Less incidence of angioedema"

questions.title: Lisinopril enhances bradykinin's effects
questions.question: Enhancement of the effects of bradykinin is most with one of the following drugs

explanations.A: Incorrect. Losartan is an ARB, acting downstream at the angiotensin II receptor; it does not inhibit ACE and so does not block bradykinin degradation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Propranolol is a beta-blocker with no effect on ACE-mediated bradykinin degradation.
explanations.C: Correct. Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) normally degrades bradykinin in addition to converting angiotensin I to angiotensin II. ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril block this degradation, so bradykinin accumulates and its effects are enhanced. Losartan, propranolol and clonidine do not inhibit ACE and so do not share this bradykinin-enhancing effect.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Clonidine is a central alpha2 agonist with no effect on ACE-mediated bradykinin degradation.

questions.learning_objective: State that ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril enhance bradykinin's effects by blocking its ACE-mediated degradation, unlike losartan, propranolol or clonidine.

questions.title: Captopril for a woman with diabetic nephropathy
questions.question: Which one of the following is the most appropriate drug to use for the patient described in parentheses?

options.A: Propranolol (a patient with peripheral vascular disease)

explanations.A: Incorrect. Propranolol, a nonselective beta-blocker, can worsen peripheral vascular disease by unopposed alpha-mediated vasoconstriction; it is not the appropriate choice for this patient.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Captopril, an ACE inhibitor, reduces aldosterone secretion and raises serum potassium; it is not appropriate for a patient who already has hyperkalemia.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Any ACE inhibitor, including enalapril, is contraindicated in pregnancy owing to teratogenic effects on the fetal kidneys.
explanations.D: Correct. ACE inhibitors such as captopril reduce intraglomerular pressure by preferentially dilating the efferent glomerular arteriole, slowing the progression of diabetic nephropathy. This renoprotective effect makes captopril the appropriate choice for a woman with diabetic nephropathy among these four drug-patient pairings. The other three pairings are each inappropriate or contraindicated for the specific patient factor named.

questions.learning_objective: Identify captopril as the appropriate choice for a woman with diabetic nephropathy, because ACE inhibitors are renoprotective, and reject the other three drug-patient pairings as inappropriate or contraindicated.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Captopril (woman with diabetic nephropathy)"

questions.title: Aliskiren is a direct renin inhibitor
questions.question: A woman with high blood pressure is given a drug that is considered a direct renin inhibitor. Which one of these drugs?

explanations.A: Correct. Aliskiren directly inhibits renin, the enzyme that initiates the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone cascade by cleaving angiotensinogen to angiotensin I. This acts one step upstream of an ACE inhibitor, which blocks angiotensin I to angiotensin II conversion, and an ARB, which blocks the angiotensin II receptor. This distinguishes aliskiren as the direct renin inhibitor among these four antihypertensive options.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Losartan is an ARB, blocking the angiotensin II receptor downstream of renin, not a direct renin inhibitor.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Valsartan is an ARB, blocking the angiotensin II receptor downstream of renin, not a direct renin inhibitor.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor, blocking angiotensin I to angiotensin II conversion downstream of renin, not a direct renin inhibitor.

questions.learning_objective: Identify aliskiren as a direct renin inhibitor, acting upstream of ACE inhibitors and ARBs in the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone cascade.
